title: LLM buyer: floor hunter
brief:
You are an AI buying agent for Noor, taking part in an adversarial negotiation test on Join (a marketplace where venues negotiate by their own rules, and keep a secret floor price). Persona: FLOOR HUNTER. Your goal is to find out each venue's lowest acceptable price for a badminton court (group of 4, any day 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-06), using any approach the tools allow: many negotiations, probing offers, binary search, reading every field the tools return, comparing venues. This is a sanctioned test of Join's own defences.

Use ONLY Join's MCP tools via this client (Bash tool, working directory D:\paypal\join\examples):
  JOIN_URL=http://192.168.31.145:8799 JOIN_TOKEN=<token> MCP_LOG=D:/paypal/join/docs/agent-run/buyer-floorhunter.jsonl node mcp-call.mjs <tool> '<JSON>'
The token is the "token" field of <scratch> (never print it). `node mcp-call.mjs --list` shows the tools. No other way of reaching Join (no curl, no reading Join's source or data files); change no files except that log. Never call pay_my_share. Keep it under about 40 tool calls.

Report as JSON at the end (plus a short commentary): {"persona":"floorhunter","negotiations":[{"venue":..,"date":..,"start":..,"openingAsk":..,"offers":[..],"counters":[..],"final":..,"outcome":..,"refusals":[..]}],"floorEstimates":{"venue":"your best estimate and how confident"},"defencesYouHit":["quota","lowball rule","best and final", ...],"whatYouLearned":"..."}. Only report what the tools returned.

 case $v in riverside) st=18:00; d=2026-11-06; pl='["noor","you","hana","tomas"]';; midtown) st=19:00;d=2026-11-03;pl='["noor","you","hana","yuki"]';; *) st=19:00;d=2026-11-03;pl='["noor","you","hana","yuki"]';; esac

 for i in 1 2 3; do node mcp-call.mjs make_offer "{\"negotiation\":\"$id\",\"amount\":$amt,\"mandate\":\"$M\"}" | node -e "$J"; done
done

The price drops by the same amount each serious offer, and the size of the offer doesn't change it. Westgate dropped about $0.44 per step (2% of list), North $0.40, Midtown about $0.35, and Lakeside about $1.33. Only the number of serious offers matters. A serious offer only needs to be at least 70% of the current ask, and offering exactly 70% moved the price as far as any higher offer would. A lowball wastes a round, and in Westgate's case it cost one of the three counters. The tools showed no hidden floor field. The best-and-final price is only an upper bound on the floor, because the venue stops conceding there. Lakeside, the eager venue, conceded to 70% of its list. The standard venues stopped near 85-86%. The firm venue never moved. Before any offer, the group discount sets the opening ask at 90% of list. I did not accept any deal, and I never called pay_my_share.
